reason: Verified in source and in the driven page, judged only on the wording and derivation of the sentence. render-b.js:215 is a string literal — "Last change: the invitations moved seven days closer." — with no accessor in it. Two distinct defects follow. (1) Number grammar. Every other quantity this product prints is a figure: the stepper readout 23px away reads "in 23 days", the steppers beside it are labelled "−7" and "+7", the away column prints bare 16/16/37/44, the horizon prints "Nothing is planned for the next 16 days." and the past block "2 done". The one spelled-out number elsewhere, "One thing is not going ahead.", is sentence-initial, which is the correct convention and confirms rather than contradicts the rule. So "seven days" is the only mid-sentence quantity in the direction set in words, and it sits inside the same 200px field of view as a control literally labelled −7 — the same quantity in two grammars at once. The file argues this exact principle against itself at line 234: "The column has one header and one grammar; writing 'in 16' into the one row you just touched gives that row a second grammar nobody asked for." Figures elsewhere also carry .num (tabular-nums, shell.css:122); this sentence carries no figure to tag. (2) Derivation. The sentence is not built from what happened and cannot be. It paints on first load before any input, and after clicking −7 the readout correctly repaints to "in 16 days" while the bar still reads "seven days closer" — measured, identical string before and after. Even the object is wrong-by-paraphrase: the fixture title is "Send the invitations", the bar says "the invitations". A status region (role="status") that announces a past-tense fact the app has no record of is the one sentence in an owner surface that must be true, and it is the only sentence in the direction that is decorative prose rather than a reading of state. Not taste, not gate-covered (neither audit.mjs nor interaction-check.mjs inspects copy derivation), and the fix breaks no palette, weight or architecture constraint.
sharpenedFix: Scope this finding to the sentence; leave the reversal wiring to the undo-behaviour finding. In render-b.js, hoist a lastMove record into the owner-editing closure and have move(delta) write { title: target.title, days: Math.abs(delta), dir: delta < 0 ? 'closer' : 'later' } into it, then repaint the bar. Do not render .b-undo at all until lastMove is set — an unfired reversibility bar has nothing true to say. When it does render, build the text from the record and set the quantity as a figure in its own tagged span so it inherits tabular-nums like every other number on the page: h("span", {}, [text "Last change: " + lastMove.title + " moved ", h("span.num", { text: String(lastMove.days) }), text " day" + (lastMove.days === 1 ? "" : "s") + " " + lastMove.dir + "."]). Use the item's own title verbatim ("Send the invitations"), not a paraphrase, so the bar names the same object the row does. Keep the singular case correct — a −1 press must read "1 day closer", never "1 days".
